 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While the New York Yankees' general manager Brian Cashman prepared to brave the cold for the 15th annual "Sleep Out," he delivered a rather cryptic message.
 His statement raised eyebrows, leaving many to wonder if a potential deal is in the works.
 Cashman stirred the pot with his statement — what did he mean by that ?
 Yankees' Brian Cashman Delivers Ambiguous Message
 GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – APRIL 08: New York Yankees General Manager Brian Cashman speaks to the media prior to the start of the game against the Boston Red Sox at Yankee Stadium on April 08, 2022 in New York City. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images)
 SNY Yankees spoke to Cashman ahead of his "Sleep Out."
 In conversation, he acknowledged the seemingly fast-paced nature of the offseason this year, but he also created buzz about a possible deal.
 "Normally the winter doesn't move as fast as it seems to be moving right now," he said, per SNY Yankees. "Who knows, I could've gotten a deal already done today. Not saying I do, not saying I don't, but we'll see."
 It's perfectly reasonable to assume Cashman is simply ruffling some feathers amid the chaos. At the same time, maybe he's hinting at something more.
 GettyWEST PALM BEACH, FLORIDA – MARCH 12: New York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman talks on the phone prior to a Grapefruit League spring training game between the Washington Nationals and the New York Yankees at FITTEAM Ballpark of The Palm Beaches on March 12, 2020 in West Palm Beach, Florida. Many professional and college sports are canceling or postponing their games due to the ongoing threat of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) outbreak. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images)
 New York is actively looking to bolster its bullpen and infield, likely in that order.
 What We Know About the Yankees' Hot Stove Season So Far
 GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – OCTOBER 07: Spencer Jones #78 of the New York Yankees runs around third base and scores a run against the Tampa Bay Rays during the third inning in game three of the American League Division Series at Yankee Stadium on October 07, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)
 As of Nov. 19, Brendan Kuty of The Athletic reported that Cashman has revealed trade interest regarding 25-year-old Spencer Jones.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "He's someone that teams are asking a lot about, and I can understand why," Cashman said. "I'm not here to say if he's our center fielder or not. I just think we're going to remain opportunistic in the marketplace and see what's available."
 Aside from Jones, top names, including Silver Slugger Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Gold Glove recipient Trent Grisham , are still exploring in free agency.
 GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 04: Jazz Chisholm Jr. #13 of the New York Yankees in action during the game against the St. Louis Cardinals at Yankee Stadium on August 04, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. The Yankees won 2-0. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)
 With such notable exits and entrances on the verge of coming to fruition, Cashman's mysterious comments could be pointing to a handful of avenues.
 A deal could be in limbo, but in the meantime, Cashman will be braving the cold at Yankee Stadium for his annual charity "Sleep Out."
